paper_title: Spatial cellular architecture predicts prognosis in glioblastoma
prediction_task: Glioblastoma prognosis prediction from spatial transcriptomics + H&E histology features

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: No molecular definition provided for glioblastoma — training data likely contains IDH-mutant tumors, and TCGA data likely contains entities no longer diagnosed as glioblastoma. These samples should be removed.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added IDH status filtering and removed non-GBM entities.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Multivariate analysis only includes the five cell-type states. Should include other prognostic factors like patient age and tumour size. Even if states no longer significant, findings are still important.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added age and tumor size to multivariate model.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: TCGA clinical annotation is limited — survival data should be treated with more caution. Number of slides in training data is relatively low.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added caveats about TCGA annotation quality and discussed sample size limitations.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Line 321: 'Genes related to low aggressiveness associated with neuronal development' could be due to lower tumor purity rather than biology. Tumor purity not accounted for.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added tumor purity analysis as confounder.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Discussion is mainly a recap of results with no discussion of study limitations or comparative efforts.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added limitations and comparison with existing AI approaches.

reviewer_strengths.text: Combining spatial transcriptomic data with imaging features on H&E sections is a very interesting and innovative approach providing new insights.
